Man and his adult son killed in Cessna collision with F-16

A relative says her brother and nephew were killed when an F-16 fighter jet smashed into their small plane, just days after another sibling was slain. Connie Stallworth says her brother Jim Johnson died just days earlier. Authorities say he and his wife, Beverly, were slain by their grandson, who has been charged with second-degree murder. Berkeley County Coroner Bill Salisbury says 68-year-old Michael Johnson was a passenger in the Cessna destroyed in the collision with the F-16. Stallworth says he was her brother. Authorities are still looking for the body of Michael Johnson's 30-year-old son Joseph. Stallworth says she is "dumbfounded that it happened twice in a few days."

What is currently being decided for the blocksize debate? I never watched the mempool until this last attack, and now I see that the mempool is staying up around 60MB... that will take forever to clear those transactions at the 1000 satoshi fee. I don't feel like we are big enough yet, to be able to let go of the perk of "transferring UNLIMITED money for NO FEE." Very little fee, just doesn't sound as good. Is Gavin planning on raising it anytime soon? I say bring on the fork while adoption is still where it is before we fork and a lot of people that haven't been around very long give up on us because we inundated them with too much information with a hard fork immediately after them jumping on the bandwagon. I think we'll leave a bad taste in some of the people's mouths who are jumping on board now. It's starting to become more than nerd money now...
What's being done about the block size debate?

What I've heard is Gavin in on vacation, coming back next week and Mike Hearn has submitted a few fixes to Gavin's block size increase code. Once it's all done they'll be adding it to Bitcoin XT and moving forward with it. At least that's the latest from Mike Hearn.

Very little fee, just doesn't sound as good

We are already at "very little fee" stage, I don't think zero-fee tx goes through very well even during non-stressed times.

I haven't had a single problem since the attack started. I pay 0.0005 BTC in fees and I'd pay more if needed. Bitcoin works fine.

transferring UNLIMITED money for NO FEE

People wanting free stuff amuse me. There is no such thing as free lunch.

Even 0.0005 is pretty high. Anything above 0.0001 ought to get you confirmed pretty quickly right now. Agreed, bitcoin works fine, but we need our wallets and services to be more aware of fee priorities.
It's a pretty contentious issue. I'm not sure it will be settled anytime soon.

Is Gavin planning on raising it anytime soon? I say bring on the fork...

It's not up to Gavin. His job right now is to convince everyone else that his plan is the best solution. So far, that hasn't happened. Increasing the blocksize will probably happen eventually, but it needs to be carefully considered and rigorously debated. It's not the sort of thing you want to rush into without taking all possible risks into account.

Also, I know people are worried about the number of unconfirmed transactions. It's certainly not ideal, but I don't believe raising the block size would solve the underlying spam issue. It would just make a cheap attack slightly more expensive. We can already make the attack more expensive without risking a careless hard fork. Transactions are confirming normally with a slightly increased transaction fee.
